metadata.title: Five Products. One Name.
metadata.purpose: Explain what each of the five Claude products (Chat, Code, Projects, Skills, Cowork) actually does and where it fits so viewers stop confusing them.

beats.narration_text: Five products, one name. They look identical from the outside but they do different things, cost different amounts, and are the wrong tool for each other's jobs. Let's map them.

card.sub: Chat · Code · Projects · Skills · Cowork — each does a different job at a different cost.

beats.narration_text: Chat is the simplest. You type a prompt, Claude replies. It's like a chatbot. How to set up: create a Gmail account for free, go to claude.ai. Biggest mistake: people try to use Chat for everything and wonder why Claude forgets context between sessions. To explain to a non-technical person: it's a back-and-forth conversation — every new chat starts fresh.

beats.narration_text: Code: you describe what you want built — Claude writes all the code, creates files, and runs it. How to set it up: click the Code tab, go to Chat, go to Cowork. It costs ten dollars a month. Biggest mistake: not giving Claude the full picture so it spends time exploring your files instead of building. Explain it to someone non-technical: a building contractor for digital things.

beats.narration_text: Projects: a saved workspace where Claude always knows your brand, your files, your context — without you re-explaining it. Click 'Projects' in the sidebar, create a new project, add your files. Biggest mistake: treating Projects like a folder — it is not a folder. It's a trained assistant that already knows everything in that project. Non-technical: like a new employee who has already read the company handbook.

beats.narration_text: Skills: an instruction manual for one thing, built in plain text, triggered by a slash command. Built in plain text in Excel, Word, or Notion. Upload it to Claude. Biggest mistake: trying to put too many things into one skill — one skill, one job. Non-technical: a recipe card. You follow it the same way every time. Skills don't pollute other chats.

beats.narration_text: Cowork: the most powerful and most expensive. It organizes your files, browses the web, runs your computer, handles research, does analysis. How to set up: click 'Projects' in the left sidebar. Biggest mistake: dumping all your files in before you start — Claude reads everything before every task, which burns tokens. Non-technical: a chief of staff who can also use your computer.

beats.narration_text: Here is the quick map: Chat for a quick question. Skills for anything you do repeatedly. Projects for everything that needs your brand context. Code for building things. Cowork for deep work with your files and the web. Match the product to the job and you stop paying Cowork prices for Chat-level work.

illustration.concept: Five-product summary row. Five small tiles in a horizontal strip, each labelled with the product name and a one-line use case: Chat → quick question; Skills → repeating tasks; Projects → brand context; Code → building things; Cowork → deep work. A small arrow under each tile points to a cost tier indicator: light / medium / medium / medium / heavy.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open Claude right now. Look at the left sidebar — what product are you actually in? Try opening one you have never used. If you have only ever used Chat, open Projects. Add one file. See what changes. The biggest unlock is usually realizing you've been paying for Cowork and running Chat tasks inside it.
